5. [Maximum mark: 16]
The function $f$ with domain $\left[0,\frac{\pi}{2}\right]$ is defined by $f(x)=\cos x+\sqrt{3}\sin x$.
This function may also be expressed in the form $R\cos(x-\alpha)$ where $R>0$ and $0<\alpha<\frac{\pi}{2}$.
(a) Find the exact value of $R$ and of $\alpha$. [3 marks]
(b) (i) Find the range of the function $f$.
(ii) State, giving a reason, whether or not the inverse function of $f$ exists. [5 marks]
(c) Find the exact value of $x$ satisfying the equation $f(x)=\sqrt{2}$. [3 marks]
(d) Using the result $\int\sec x\,\mathrm{d}x=\ln|\sec x+\tan x|+C$, where $C$ is a constant, show that $\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{f(x)}=\frac{1}{2}\ln\left(3+2\sqrt{3}\right)$. [5 marks]

sequence.
